q-51960.name: Question 3
q-51960.problem: Find, in point-slope form, the equation of the line that passes through the points $(2,4)$  and $(-4,-8).$
q-51960.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the point $(2,4),$ so we can use $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(2,4)$ in our point-slope formula. All that remains is to compute $m,$ and we can do this using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}=\frac{(-8)-4}{(-4)-2}=\frac{-12}{-6}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $m=2$ and the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(2,4)$ into the point-slope formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-4 & =2(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$
